prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a top-down close-up view where a person's bare forearm and hand (with henna designs) stretch horizontally from left to right across the foreground at roughly 0.25–0.4 m from the camera wearer, while the camera wearer's own hands work immediately below and against that arm at roughly 0.2–0.35 m. Directly beneath the outstretched arm is the camera wearer's patterned lap at about 0.5–0.6 m, flanked by red fabric on the upper left (0.5–0.8 m) and a dark floor surface on the upper right (~0.8–1.0 m) where a cell phone, a henna cone, and cotton rest alongside a third seated person's skirt edge in the top background (~1.0–1.2 m). All visible hands, the outstretched arm, and the floor items remain within arm's reach of both the camera wearer and the person extending their arm, with the outstretched forearm partially occluding the camera wearer's left hand, lap, and cotton ball beneath it. Across the five frames, the viewpoint pulls back slightly from Frame 1 to Frames 2–4 (revealing the full spread hand on the right and making the foreground arm slightly dimmer/farther) as the wearer's left hand reaches up to the floor in Frame 2 and returns under the arm in Frames 3–4, before moving closer again in Frame 5. The depth map clearly separates the elevated horizontal arm and active hands from the patterned lap and cluttered floor in a way that is visually busy in RGB, though it is unreliable on flat floor objects like the cell phone and small henna cone, which nearly vanish into the dark background plane.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map labels parts of the scene in the foreground and midground—such as the horizontal arm, the camera wearer's lap and hands (~0.2–0.6 m), and the red fabric on the left (~0.5–0.8 m)—as `person` masks, while detecting the cell phone on the upper-right floor (~0.8–1.0 m) in Frames 1, 2, 4, and 5. In Frame 1 and Frame 5, it splits the upper-left red garment and the horizontal foreground arm into two distinct `person` masks, and in Frame 2 it isolates the camera wearer's lower-right hand as a separate `person` mask from the main arm and hand cluster. Across the five frames, the `cell phone` mask shifts position and scale in the upper-right quadrant as the camera wearer's head tilts up in Frames 2–4 and back down in Frame 5, while every person's torso and head remain completely out of the top-down field of view so gaze toward the wearer cannot be seen. While segmentation reliably localizes the rectangular boundary of the cell phone on the floor in most frames, it is highly unreliable overall: in Frames 3 and 4 it merges the outstretched arm, the camera wearer's hands and lap, the left-side red clothing, and the top-background seated person into a single giant `person` mask that obscures all occlusions and boundaries between individuals. It also hallucinates a `dog` label on the white cotton ball in Frame 1, mislabels part of the cell phone and spread fingers as a `laptop` in Frame 4, and misses the cell phone entirely in Frame 3 as well as the henna cones in all frames.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is completely black across all five frames, detecting zero body or hand skeletons anywhere in the scene. In the RGB strip, the scene contains an outstretched bare left forearm and spread hand extending from the left at roughly 0.25–0.4 m, the camera wearer's own two hands working from the bottom edge at 0.2–0.35 m (holding a henna cone on the right and a cotton ball on the left), and the lower legs/skirt of another seated person at the top edge (~1.0–1.2 m). Because all upper torsos, shoulders, and heads are outside the close-up downward-angled field of view, neither the RGB image nor the pose map can directly show head orientation or whether anyone is looking at the camera wearer, though body placement indicates the wearer faces downward, the person extending their arm sits to the left, and the third person sits in front. Across the five frames, the camera wearer's left hand moves from holding the underside of the forearm (Frame 1) to picking up cotton on the floor (Frame 2), dabbing beneath the forearm (Frames 3–4), and supporting the arm again (Frame 5), while the right hand applies or holds the henna cone near the lower edge. The pose map contributes no spatial information beyond RGB and is completely unreliable here because the extreme egocentric close-up, heavy cropping of torsos and heads, henna patterns on the skin, and mutual hand-on-arm occlusions cause the skeleton detector to fail entirely.
